outcome: No result found in the window (26 Jan 2024 – present) that bears on the question of whether there exist three unknotted space curves, not all circles, that cannot be arranged to form the Borromean rings. All foundational work on this question (Freedman–Skora's 1987 proof that circles alone cannot form the rings, Cook's conjecture that any three unknotted curves not all circles can, Cantarella's proposed counterexample, and Howards' 2013/2014 weakening of the conjecture to planar curves) predates the frozen revision. Recent Borromean-rings papers found in the window address unrelated questions (hyperbolic geometry of the complement, ellipse-linking detection algorithms, quantum vortex dynamics, link Floer homology, gordian unknots under thickness constraints).
summary: Wikipedia's stated open problem is: 'Are there three unknotted curves, not all circles, that cannot form the Borromean rings?' — this is the open converse of Cook's conjecture (that any three unknotted simple closed curves, not all circles, CAN be combined to form the Borromean rings), as weakened by Hugh Howards after Jason Cantarella proposed a possible counterexample (a specific torus-parameterized curve). All of that history — Freedman–Skora's 1987 impossibility result for circles, Cook's conjecture, Cantarella's proposed counterexample, and Howards' 2013/2014 paper 'Forming the Borromean Rings out of arbitrary polygonal unknots' proving the planar-curve case — predates the 26 January 2024 frozen revision and is out of scope. I searched extensively for any 2024–2026 work addressing this specific realizability question: direct searches on Cook's conjecture, Howards' name, Cantarella's proposed counterexample, arXiv listings for 'Borromean rings' across 2024–2026, and MathOverflow/survey-style queries. I found several genuinely new arXiv papers touching Borromean rings in the window (2404.02615 on the hyperbolic geometry of the Borromean rings complement; 2405.20874 on Borromean hypergraphs in random rectangles/percolation; 2506.04442 on 'gordian unknots' under curvature/thickness constraints, unrelated to this question as the triage also found; 2509.15104 on an efficient algorithm to detect Hopf/Borromean linking between ellipses, a computational-geometry question about a specific curve family rather than Cook's general realizability question; 2507.20903 on energy minimization of topological links; a February 2025 paper on quantum vortex Borromean-ring dynamics governed by the Gross-Pitaevskii equation; and an August 2026 paper on link Floer homology of the Borromean rings). None of these engage with the stated question of whether some non-circular unknotted triple fails to realize the Borromean link. I therefore agree with the triage verdict of 'none' and confirm status open with no_change_found true.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2509.15104 ellipse-linking-detection paper is adjacent, since ellipses are a natural non-circular curve family relevant to Cook's conjecture and Howards' planar-curve case; but the paper is a computational/algorithmic contribution to detecting whether given ellipses ARE linked, not a realizability or counterexample result bearing on the open question, so I classified it as out of scope.
what_would_settle_it: A paper (or proof) either exhibiting a specific non-circular unknotted triple that cannot be arranged into the Borromean link (settling the question affirmatively, likely building on Cantarella's proposed torus counterexample), or a general proof that every non-circular unknotted triple can always be so arranged (proving Cook's conjecture in full and thereby resolving the stated question negatively).
